title: Scalar extension of the canonically transported constant module sheaf
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $R$ a commutative ring, $B$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\alpha:\underline R_{\mathrm{Comm}}\to B$ a ring-sheaf morphism, using constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For an $R$-module $P$, form its constant module sheaf [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor] and transport its coefficient ring from $\underline R_{\mathrm{Ring}}$ to the underlying ring of $\underline R_{\mathrm{Comm}}$ along the canonical ring isomorphism [def-sfb-constant-module-coefficient-transport]; denote this transported module by $F_{\mathrm{Comm}}(P)$. Define $C_B(P)$ to be the ordinary scalar extension of $F_{\mathrm{Comm}}(P)$ along $\alpha$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], a sheaf of modules over the underlying ring of $B$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Explicitly it is the module sheafification of $U\mapsto B(U)\otimes_{\underline R_{\mathrm{Comm}}(U)}F_{\mathrm{Comm}}(P)(U)$. For an $R$-linear map $f:P\to Q$, define $C_B(f)$ by the induced scalar-extension map, sending a local tensor $b\otimes x$ to $b\otimes F_{\mathrm{Comm}}(f)(x)$. The notation $b\otimes p\in C_B(P)(U)$ means the canonical pure-tensor section [def-sfb-scalar-extension-pure-tensor-section] applied to the constant-section unit $\eta_P(p)\in F_{\mathrm{Comm}}(P)(U)$ and $b\in B(U)$. No finite generation, projectivity or flatness is required for these constructions.
